plan: This is a single-round auction with three bidders. My value is $22. To maximize profit, I need to win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid. I will bid slightly above what I believe the second-highest bid will be. Given the range of possible values (0-49), a conservative approach is to bid around $11, aiming to win against bids likely to be below that, while avoiding overpaying.

Given this is the final round, a conservative strategy is best. My value is $34. I want to win if the second highest bid is below $34. To ensure this, I should bid slightly above what I expect the others to bid, but not excessively. I will bid $34.10. The worst case is someone bids $34.20+, and I lose, paying nothing. A lower bid risks losing to a bid I *would* have won against.

My value is $10. To maximize profit, I need to win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll adopt a conservative strategy. Bidding slightly above a reasonable estimate of the second-highest bid is prudent. I'll bid $6.10. This ensures I win if the other bids are below $6.10, and my profit will be positive (10 - second highest bid). A higher bid risks overpaying.
